title: Base64 decoding: validated errors and zero retries
subtitle: Real Scala calls, two revisions, and offline parameter controls.
background:
Skip if you know this already

Base64 stores bytes as printable text. Decoding can fail when the input is malformed. A Scala Either makes a valid result and a rejected input explicit values.

The part that changes

The original decoder rejected every call with zero retries and allowed malformed input to throw. The new decoder treats zero as an initial attempt, rejects negative retries, and returns validation errors as Left values. The generated harness runs both revisions against identical inputs.
intuition: Zero retries still permits one attempt. An empty input now has its own validation error.
